learning_outcomes.text: Provide students with the fundamental theoretical models and operational tools for the study of biomechanical structural systems composed of continuous bodies, with particular reference to structural elements that can be modeled as beams.
Analyze the conditions of equilibrium, compatibility, constitutive behavior, strength, and stability within the framework of solid mechanics.
Provide a rigorous formulation of the mechanical models used in structural analysis in the field of biomechanics, building upon the knowledge of Mathematics and Physics acquired in previous years.
Foster a critical approach to modeling and solving concrete problems, with particular attention to the consistency of the adopted assumptions and to the range of validity of the models employed.

syllabus_topics: INTRODUCTION TO THE THEORY OF ELASTIC STRUCTURES
ELASTIC BEAM THEORY AND STATICALLY INDETERMINATE BEAM SYSTEMS
ENGINEERING BEAM THEORY – THE DE SAINT-VENANT SOLID
CONSTITUTIVE MODELS IN BIOENGINEERING AND BIOMECHANICS
